summary: In Greek legend, Leonymus (also told as Autoleon) is a general of Croton in Magna Graecia. When he tries to force the vacant place left for Ajax in the Locrian battle-line, the hero's shade wounds him; an oracle sends him to Achilles' White Island (Leuce) in the Euxine, where he is healed and sees Helen, who commissions Stesichorus' palinode. Pausanias names him Leonymus; Conon and others Autoleon.

sections.heading: Wound from Ajax
paragraphs: In war between Croton and the Locrians of Italy, the Locrians leave one place open in their ranks for their national hero Ajax. Leonymus presses into that gap hoping to break them; the phantom of Ajax appears and inflicts a grievous wound.
The oracle bids him propitiate Ajax with sacrifice on the island of Leuce. He sails there, is cured, and becomes the first man legend credits with reaching Achilles' White Island.

sections.heading: Helen and Stesichorus
paragraphs: On Leuce he also sees Helen, who sends a message to Stesichorus: the poet, blinded after blaming her, will recover his sight if he retracts. Stesichorus composes the famous palinode in her praise and is healed.
Pausanias tells the Crotoniate as Leonymus; the same voyage is attached to Autoleon in other authors. The atlas follows Pausanias' name.
